body.p: Claim 17 was objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but was indicated as allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Applicant thanks the Examiner for the indication of allowable subject matter.

In the Office Action, claims 12, and 15 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) and 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Gagnon et al. (US 10,093,419 B2). Claims 1-3, 5, 16 and 18 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke et al. (US 6,016,016) in view of Gagnon. Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Gagnon and further in view of Sharma (US 2017/0066534). Claims 6, 8-9 and 11 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Gagnon and further in view of Mattes (US 2004/0048582). Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Mattes and Klose et al. (US 2018/079507). Claim 10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Gagnon, in view of Mattes and further in view of Sharma. Claim 10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Gagnon, in view of Mattes, and further in view of Francois et al. (US 8,321,611 B2). Claims 13-14 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Gagnon in view of Sharma. Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing rejections and requests reconsideration.

Applicant has amended claims 1 and 12 to include the allowable subject matter of claim 17. Accordingly, claims 1 and 12 are now in condition for allowance, and withdrawal of Section 102 and 103 rejections are respectfully requested.
Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application should be found to be allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the
claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

The amendments to the claims were done merely to expedite prosecution of the present case. Applicant reserves any and all rights to pursue the subject matter of the original claims in this application, or in another application. Moreover, these amendments should not be construed as an admission or acquiescence to any rejection.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rejections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be required to this application under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16-1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 07-2069.
Should the Examiner discover there are remaining issues which may be resolved by a telephone interview, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney at (312) 600-6841.
